comparison_100task_run.note: No collapse at 100 tasks either; 300-task extension confirms result

subject_executed: Online Permuted-MNIST, 3-layer MLP (784→2000→2000→10, ReLU), SGD lr=0.05 momentum=0.9 WD=0.0, no plasticity repair, 300 tasks × 1000 steps/task × 3 seeds. 4 observables tracked per task: dead_unit_fraction (>95% threshold, both hidden layers averaged), effective_rank (penultimate layer SVD entropy), gradient_noise_scale (McCandlish B_opt, 2×64 mini-batches), weight_norm_drift (per-layer relative change from init). LR=0.05 reused from prior pmnist 100-task tuning run. MNIST downloaded via torchvision to /tmp/mnist. Run on NVIDIA H100 80GB. Script: src/run_pml2.py.
notes: ANSWER: NO — a healthy net (task1_acc=0.975, dead_after_t1=0.023) does NOT lose plasticity at 300 permuted-MNIST tasks. acc_drop from first-20 to last-20 tasks = 0.41pp (trivial). 0/3 seeds met the collapse criterion (≥15pp drop, ≥2 consecutive tasks). This extends the prior 100-task result (0.16pp drop) to 300 tasks. Dead-unit fraction grew 33× (0.023→0.75) without causing accuracy collapse. Effective rank INCREASED from ~256 to ~381 (network becomes MORE diverse, not less). Gradient-noise scale was stable throughout (1.5–2.2 range). Weight-norm drift grew to 33× initial norm. No precedence analysis possible (no collapse to date). INTERPRETATION: Permuted-MNIST with SGD+momentum is not a good benchmark for plasticity loss — same label set across tasks, label-preserving permutations, large hidden width (2000). Loss of plasticity requires incompatible task distributions (split tasks) or more aggressive training. Dohare et al. collapse requires split-CIFAR or label-incompatible streams. This finding is consistent with but extends the prior pmnist run; honest negative result.
